title: BIGBANG Is Back — 20th Anniversary World Tour, Coachella, and YG's Full 2026 Masterplan Revealed
excerpt: YG Entertainment just unveiled its entire 2026 roadmap: BIGBANG's 20th anniversary world tour, a confirmed Coachella appearance, and a new boy group debut. Yang Hyun-suk delivered the announcement personally.
author: MEARROW Editorial Desk
content:
On March 4th, YG Entertainment dropped a bombshell on its official YouTube channel: the company's full 2026 business roadmap. One unannounced video shook the entire K-pop fandom. BIGBANG's 20th anniversary global tour confirmed. Coachella appearance locked in. A new boy group debut — YG's first male idol group since TREASURE. And the most surprising part? Yang Hyun-suk himself sat in front of the camera to deliver every word.

## BIGBANG: The 20-Year Legends Return to the Stage

### 'BIGSHOW: REBORN' — A Legacy Tour

BIGBANG's (G-Dragon, Taeyang, Daesung) global world tour 'BIGSHOW: REBORN' is officially confirmed. Twenty years after their 2006 debut, the group with the longest career in K-pop history is returning to the stage.

BIGBANG's last official tour was the 'LAST DANCE' tour in 2017–2018. What followed was a cascade of disruptions: military enlistments, Seungri's departure, and G-Dragon's drug investigation (which ended with no charges filed). For eight years, group activities were effectively frozen. G-Dragon's successful 2025 solo comeback laid the foundation for this reunion tour.

| Detail | Information |
|--------|------------|
| Tour Name | BIGSHOW: REBORN |
| Members | G-Dragon, Taeyang, Daesung (3 members) |
| Scale | Global World Tour |
| Key Date | Coachella 2026 confirmed |
| Expected Start | Second half of 2026 |

### Coachella 2026 — K-pop Legends on America's Biggest Stage

BIGBANG's Coachella 2026 appearance was confirmed simultaneously. This isn't just a festival booking — Coachella is the global music industry's benchmark for cultural relevance. If BLACKPINK made history as Coachella headliners in 2023, BIGBANG's appearance proves that first-generation K-pop legends still command the global stage.

G-Dragon's 2025 solo activities already reignited his visibility in the American market. YG's strategy is clear: channel that momentum into BIGBANG as a unit and detonate it at Coachella.

## YG's Next Generation: First New Boy Group Since TREASURE

### Fall 2026: A New Male Idol Group Debuts

YG announced a new boy group debut for fall 2026 — the company's first male idol launch in six years, since TREASURE's 2020 debut. This fills the most significant gap in YG's current artist portfolio.

A look at YG's active idol lineup makes the situation clear:

| Group | Gender | Debut | Current Status |
|-------|--------|-------|---------------|
| BIGBANG | Male | 2006 | 20th anniversary tour planned |
| TREASURE | Male | 2020 | Active |
| BLACKPINK | Female | 2016 | Individual activities focus |
| BABYMONSTER | Female | 2023 | Rapidly growing |
| **New Boy Group** | **Male** | **Fall 2026** | **Debut planned** |

BIGBANG can't tour forever, and TREASURE alone isn't enough to compete in the male idol market. HYBE runs a three-group male system (TXT, ENHYPEN, SEVENTEEN). JYP has Stray Kids and NEXZ. YG needs a next-generation boy group to stay in the race.

### 'NEXT MONSTER' — BABYMONSTER Sub-Unit

Another intriguing announcement: a BABYMONSTER sub-unit tentatively called 'NEXT MONSTER'. Built around members EVELLI and CHANYA, with two additional members to join. Combined with a confirmed BABYMONSTER world tour, YG is simultaneously expanding its girl group vertical.

## What Yang Hyun-suk's Appearance Signals

The most noteworthy element of this announcement wasn't the content — it was the messenger. Yang Hyun-suk, YG's founder and chief producer, has largely stayed out of the public eye since the Burning Sun scandal in 2019. His internal influence at YG never wavered, but on-camera appearances became rare.

His decision to personally deliver the 2026 roadmap sends two messages:

1. **Confidence**: YG has recovered and is ready for aggressive expansion
2. **Leadership reaffirmation**: "I'm still steering the ship" — a signal aimed at both internal stakeholders and the broader industry

## MEARROW's Take: What YG's 2026 Strategy Really Means

From MEARROW's perspective, this announcement isn't a schedule reveal — it's a declaration. YG is re-entering the Big 3 competition at full force.

The 2024–2025 K-pop market was dominated by HYBE (BTS comeback) and JYP (Stray Kids' global expansion). SM Entertainment also made waves with aespa and NCT WISH. YG, meanwhile, had BABYMONSTER's growth trajectory and G-Dragon's solo comeback, but lacked a defining large-scale move.

This masterplan attempts to fill that gap in one stroke. BIGBANG's legacy power + BABYMONSTER's growth momentum + a new boy group's future value. Three pillars activated simultaneously, positioning YG for a full counteroffensive starting in the second half of 2026.

If it works, YG proves the "Big 3" label still means something. If it doesn't? The fundamental question resurfaces: can YG maintain its status in a post-BIGBANG era?

## The Second Half of 2026 Changes Everything

BIGBANG's return. Coachella. A new boy group. YG played every card in its hand at once. All that's left is execution. One thing is certain for K-pop fans and MEARROW league observers alike — the K-pop landscape in the second half of 2026 will look very different from today.
